_readme: Per-class decision thresholds. A probability at or above the threshold for a
class means that class fires. The six classes are independent: any number of
them can fire on the same comment.
Do not use 0.5. The rare classes (severe_toxic, threat, identity_hate) are
well ordered but badly calibrated, so a 0.5 cut throws away most of their
recall. Every threshold below sits under 0.5 for that reason.
Thresholds were chosen to maximise per-class F1 on the validation split and
are then applied unchanged to the held-out test split. They are a single
global set: there is no per-language block here, deliberately. See

_provenance.status: <<PENDING_FINAL_METRICS>> these thresholds were tuned on the PREVIOUS checkpoint and must be re-tuned against the final weights before this repo is published. This is a step to re-run, not a number to type in.
_provenance.search: grid over candidate thresholds, per class independently, maximising F1 on validation
_provenance.per_language_block_omitted: The evaluation script also emits a per-language threshold block. It is not shipped. That code path builds an unshuffled KFold instead of a stratified one, so folds containing zero positives combine with zero_division=1 to inject free F1 scores of 1.0. It reported English severe_toxic at F1 0.597 when the maximum achievable at any threshold is 0.442. Nothing in the serving path ever read it.

validation_f1_at_threshold._note: F1 achieved at the threshold above, on the validation split, by the PREVIOUS (April 2025) checkpoint. Recorded for provenance only. It is not this model's performance and it is not a test-split number.

validation_positive_support._note: Positive examples per class in the 35,658-row validation split used for tuning.
